name: Pahat-Moab
title: Leader of a returning Jewish family
summary: Pahat-Moab (meaning 'governor of Moab') was the head of a prominent Jewish family that returned from the Babylonian exile. His descendants were among the largest groups to return to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel and later under Ezra. The family played an important role in the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the renewal of the covenant with God.

keyEvents.title: The Return of the Descendants under Zerubbabel
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Pahat-Moab, through Joshua and Joab, were among the largest groups to return from Babylon to Jerusalem. They numbered 2,812 people.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Nehemiah's Register
keyEvents.description: Pahat-Moab's descendants were also listed in Nehemiah's register of those who returned from captivity, numbering 2,818 people.

keyEvents.title: Descendants Who Took Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Some of the descendants of Pahat-Moab were among those who had married foreign women and had to separate from them during Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: More Descendants Return Under Ezra
keyEvents.description: Under Ezra's leadership, an additional 200 men from the family of Pahat-Moab returned to Jerusalem from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: The Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Pahat-Moab (or a representative of the family) was among the leaders who sealed the covenant to follow God's law during Nehemiah's time.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the Wall of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Hashub, son of Pahat-Moab, helped repair part of the wall of Jerusalem and the Tower of the Ovens during Nehemiah's rebuilding project.
